newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - OUB may place more shares.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - OUB may place more shares.

text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd may sell more shares through private placements in the future if the need arises for more capital, president and chief executive officer Peter Seah said on Friday.

Seah told Reuters in an interview the bank's strategy had been, and would continue to be, to strengthen its capital base in order to enable it to maximise the business potential it saw within Singapore and the region.
OUB, one of Singapore's four main banks with total assets at the end of 1995 of Singapore $25.63 billion, has had three major private share placements over the last few years.
"Over the last five years we have raised our capital funds from about S$900 million to over S$3.0 billion today," he said.
Asked if the bank would place more shares, Seah said:
"As the need for capital continues, we have various options and one of them is to do private placements. I would say down the road, yes. I mean it is a question of when we do it."
Asked whether he could say when a placement might take place, he replied: "Definitely not."
Seah said the bank had had "a very healthy" return on equity and its earnings per share had increased, even with the private share placements.

"It underscores our basic philosophy that if we can demonstrate to shareholders that every dollar that they give to us can be put to very good use, to generate more profits for the bank without diluting the returns on the equity, then our requests for more capital should be a good thing," he said.
He said it was necessary to increase the size of the bank to allow it access to the whole range of banking operations.

"We feel that if you look at the potential for the region then a capital increasing exercise is truly to position the organisation for the long-term," he said. "I think if you don't position yourself properly, then you will miss the opportunities
which exist and be unable to tap the opportunities."
Seah said the bank had been ranked recently by the International Financial Review as the number one bank for syndications in the ASEAN region.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

"For example, if OUB had stayed at S$900 million capital funds size, we would not have been able to operate as a major loan syndicator in the region because many of the banks in the region would have been larger than us," he said.

"At our current size, being the fifth largest in ASEAN in terms of capital and 162nd in the world, we can quite confidently walk into all the major banks and corporations in the region and offer them our services."
"We can fight for big mandates, whether it be for infrastructure financing or for fund-raising for major corporations," he said.
